question: A patient with a new leg cast complains of severe, burning pain that does not respond to prescribed pain medication and has pale toes. What is the nurse's priority action?

options.A: Instruct the patient to exercise their toes more vigorously
options.B: Apply a heating pad directly over the tight plaster cast
options.C: Notify the doctor immediately for signs of compartment syndrome
options.D: Wait patiently until the next scheduled pain medication time

explanation: Unrelenting pain and poor circulation under a cast can signal dangerous pressure build-up, requiring urgent medical evaluation. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T10#GNS222_U1_T10_h8)

question: Why are tiny air particles like PM2.5 so dangerous to our health?

options.A: They react with sunlight to form ozone gas
options.B: They bypass upper airway filters and reach deep lung tissues
options.C: They create a visible yellow haze over industrial cities
options.D: They dissolve completely in the saliva inside the mouth

explanation: Great job! Because they are so tiny, PM2.5 particles slip right past our nose and throat defenses and go straight into the tiny air sacs in our lungs. [learn more](GST114_U6_T7#GST114_U6_T7_h2)

question: What is pica, a condition nurses watch out for during dietary checks?

options.A: An allergic reaction to eating citrus fruits during pregnancy
options.B: An excessive thirst that leads to drinking too much water daily
options.C: A complete loss of appetite caused by severe hormonal changes
options.D: A strong craving to eat non-food items like clay, starch, or ice

explanation: Pica happens when a mum craves non-food items like chalk or clay. It's usually the body's way of whispering that she lacks certain minerals like iron! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T012#GNS227_U2_T012_h7)

question: When should a client take off a male condom after ejaculation?

options.A: Wait until the next morning to take it off
options.B: Take it off only after the erection has completely gone down
options.C: Flush it down the toilet right away
options.D: Remove it immediately while holding the base of the penis

explanation: Well done! Pulling out while still a bit erect and holding the base stops the condom from slipping and spilling semen. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h4)

question: A nurse tells a colleague, 'I feel worried about patient safety when medications are left unlabeled.' What communication trick is being used here?

options.A: Avoiding the issue by changing the subject completely
options.B: Using an 'I' statement to express concern constructively
options.C: Accommodating the colleague's poor medication habits
options.D: Using a competing strategy to assert dominance

explanation: Starting with 'I feel' keeps the focus on your observations and patient safety instead of sounding like an attack on your coworker. [learn more](GST321_U5_T4#GST321_U5_T4_h7)

question: Why should a nurse involve the client in modifying their own meal plan?

options.A: It eliminates all future health risks related to poor nutrition
options.B: It relieves the nurse from doing any paperwork during the visit
options.C: It ensures the client feels ownership and will stick to the changes
options.D: It proves that the client has a better education than the nurse

explanation: Spot on! When clients help build their own plan, they feel a sense of ownership and are much more likely to stick with it. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T004#GNS227_U3_T004_h7)

question: What nasty surprise can happen when a patient stays on broad-spectrum antibiotics for too long?

options.A: Total failure of pancreatic enzyme production
options.B: Immediate drop in visual acuity
options.C: Permanent loss of the sense of taste
options.D: Superinfection from drug-resistant opportunistic organisms

explanation: When you wipe out good flora, opportunistic bugs like fungi or *C. diff* take over and cause a superinfection. Good to keep in mind for clinicals! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T2#GNS215_U6_T2_h4)

question: What is the main difference between disease incidence and disease prevalence?

options.A: Incidence measures deaths, while prevalence measures recoveries.
options.B: Incidence counts only new cases, while prevalence counts all existing cases.
options.C: Prevalence is only used for acute infections, while incidence is for chronic illnesses.
options.D: There is no difference; both terms mean the exact same thing.

explanation: Think of incidence as new arrivals over a period, while prevalence is a snapshot of everyone currently carrying the condition at a given time. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T90#GNS214_U1_T90_h2)

question: What is the main reason we teach patients respiratory hygiene and cough etiquette?

options.A: Reducing the cost of cleaning medical equipment
options.B: Preventing foodborne illnesses among patients
options.C: Containing respiratory pathogens at the source
options.D: Purifying the air inside closed hospital wards

explanation: Spot on! Cough etiquette stops germs right where they start—catching them in a tissue or elbow before they can fly into the air. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h4)

question: What is a harmless, funny side effect you might see when a patient takes bismuth subsalicylate?

options.A: Temporary hair loss on the scalp
options.B: Bright yellow coloration of the urine
options.C: Painless whitening of the fingernails
options.D: Darkening of the stool and tongue

explanation: Don't panic! Bismuth reacts with sulfur in your gut to create a harmless dark pigment that turns the tongue and stool black. It goes away soon after stopping the drug. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T3#GNS223_U3_T3_h4)

question: Why is checking the suction apparatus considered a critical step before beginning the intubation procedure?

options.A: To inflate the balloon cuff once the tube is in the trachea
options.B: To quickly clear vomit, blood, or secretions blocking the view
options.C: To measure the exact volume of air inside the patient's lungs
options.D: To deliver humidified oxygen straight down the breathing tube

explanation: Unforeseen fluids can instantly obscure the clinician's view of the vocal cords, making immediate suction essential for patient safety. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h2)

question: Which indicator measures the final health results experienced by the patient?

options.A: Outcome indicator
options.B: Financial indicator
options.C: Process indicator
options.D: Structure indicator

explanation: Outcome indicators look at the end result—whether the patient recovered well, had complications, or improved overall. [learn more](GST321_U1_T19#GST321_U1_T19_h4)

question: Why is checking the publication date important when reading health articles online?

options.A: Older articles require special passwords to open them
options.B: Websites automatically delete articles after exactly one year
options.C: Older web pages take up too much space on computer screens
options.D: Medical guidelines and treatment practices change as new research emerges

explanation: Healthcare is fast-moving, and outdated information can lead to unsafe clinical practices or incorrect patient education. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T9#GNS113_U1_T9_h5)

question: What is the name of the middle phase of yellow fever when a patient's early symptoms temporarily disappear?

options.A: Convalescent phase
options.B: Remission phase
options.C: Intoxication phase
options.D: Viremic phase

explanation: That's correct! During the remission phase, the patient might feel like they are magically getting better before any severe symptoms hit. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T9#GNS214_U1_T9_h3)

question: What is a windshield survey during a community assessment?

options.A: An inventory of all drugs available inside the local primary health center
options.B: A laboratory test used to check the purity of drinking water sources
options.C: An observational method where the nurse travels through the community to note environmental conditions
options.D: A written examination given to school children to test their health knowledge

explanation: A windshield survey is a quick observation method where nurses drive or walk through a community to observe housing, sanitation, and resources. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T26#GNS225_U2_T26_h5)

question: Which type of isolation is used to protect a patient with a very weak immune system?

options.A: Strict contact isolation
options.B: Respiratory isolation
options.C: Protective isolation
options.D: Standard isolation

explanation: Protective or reverse isolation guards patients who cannot fight off everyday germs by keeping outside microorganisms away from them. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h3)

question: Why is a psychosocial assessment vital for clients with neurologic conditions?

options.A: Nerve damage and brain injury affect thinking, mood, and daily life.
options.B: It is the only legal way to discharge a patient from the hospital.
options.C: Physical therapy cannot start until mental health is fully cured.
options.D: It replaces the need for a standard physical doctor's examination.

explanation: Brain and nerve disorders directly alter a person's behavior, emotions, and interactions, making psychosocial evaluation just as important as physical care. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T5#GNS222_U3_T5_h1)

question: A pregnant woman at 32 weeks gestation arrives with vaginal bleeding and a rigid, painful abdomen. What is the most appropriate immediate nursing action?

options.A: Prepare the patient for an immediate routine digital cervical exam
options.B: Apply warm compresses to the lower abdomen to relieve muscle cramps
options.C: Encourage the patient to walk around to help stimulate labor progress
options.D: Notify the doctor, check vital signs, and monitor fetal heart tones

explanation: An unstable patient presenting with signs of abruption requires immediate medical notification, vital sign stabilization, and fetal surveillance while avoiding internal exams. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T017#GNS226_U2_T017_h5)

question: What is the main goal of medical treatment for someone with hyperthyroidism?

options.A: Replacing deficient thyroid hormones with synthetic T4
options.B: Blocking all adrenaline receptors in the central nervous system
options.C: Permanently destroying the thyroid gland using chemical agents
options.D: Restoring a normal metabolic state known as euthyroidism

explanation: We want to bring those high hormone levels back down to a healthy, balanced state called euthyroidism. You've got this! [learn more](GNS223_U7_T3#GNS223_U7_T3_h1)

question: When are helicopter or boat transport methods most necessary during a disaster evacuation?

options.A: When floods, landslides, or collapsed bridges block traditional roads
options.B: When the patient has a minor injury and lives next to a hospital
options.C: When hospital emergency rooms are completely empty
options.D: When ground ambulances are running low on diesel fuel only

explanation: Spot on! When roads are completely impassable due to natural disasters, air and water transport are the only ways out. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T3#GNS315_U5_T3_h7)

question: Why does metabolic acidosis happen during prolonged shock?

options.A: Cells switch to anaerobic metabolism and produce lactic acid
options.B: Carbon dioxide dissolves directly into the circulating blood plasma
options.C: The kidneys stop filtering hydrogen ions from the bloodstream
options.D: Excessive oxygen enters the cells and lowers blood pH

explanation: Great job thinking about cellular metabolism! When cells don't get enough oxygen, they switch to backup (anaerobic) energy production. This leaves behind lactic acid as waste, which lowers blood pH and causes acidosis. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T3#GNS112_U7_T3_h1)

question: How do transient microbiota differ from resident microbiota?

options.A: Transient microbes only stay on the body for a short time
options.B: Resident microbes are easily washed off with basic soap
options.C: Transient microbes permanently colonize deep internal organs
options.D: Resident microbes only survive in the body for a few hours

explanation: Think of transient microbes like temporary visitors dropping by for a quick visit. They don't stick around for long, unlike our permanent resident flora! [learn more](GST114_U3_T1#GST114_U3_T1_h2)

question: Why is it helpful for a nurse to check how much menstrual pain affects a patient's daily routine?

options.A: To determine how severely the pain interferes with the patient's life
options.B: To decide whether the patient needs immediate emergency surgery
options.C: To prove to the physician that the patient is exaggerating symptoms
options.D: To calculate the exact financial cost of missed work days

explanation: Brilliant! Understanding how much pain disrupts their day helps us gauge the severity and plan the best care. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T6#GNS216_U2_T6_h5)

question: How do grief and mourning differ from each other?

options.A: Grief is a medical diagnosis, while mourning is a nursing intervention
options.B: Grief only happens in hospitals, while mourning happens at home
options.C: Grief is the internal emotional feeling, while mourning is the outward expression
options.D: Grief lasts for years, while mourning ends after a few days

explanation: Think of grief as what happens inside your heart and mind, while mourning is how you show it on the outside through cultural or religious practices. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T10#GNS321_U4_T10_h1)

question: Why do patients with severe burns or major infections need significantly more calories than usual?

options.A: Stress hormones trigger a hypermetabolic state that dramatically increases energy demand
options.B: Intravenous antibiotic medications slow down digestion and trap extra nutrients
options.C: Bed rest completely eliminates muscle mass, lowering overall energy requirements
options.D: The skin dressings trap body heat, which stops natural calorie burning

explanation: Big physical trauma puts the body into overdrive. Stress hormones flood the system, speeding up metabolism and tissue breakdown like a raging fire. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T9#GNS121_U1_T9_h5)

question: Which spinal nerve roots combine to form the brachial plexus?

options.A: T1 through T12
options.B: C5 through T1
options.C: C1 through C4
options.D: L1 through S4

explanation: The brachial plexus is a complex web formed by the ventral rami of cervical nerves five through eight and the first thoracic nerve. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T26#GNS211_U3_T26_h5)

question: What is another common medical term for a joint?

options.A: Articulation
options.B: Cartilage plate
options.C: Ligament
options.D: Tendinous band

explanation: Spot on! In anatomy and nursing, we call a joint an articulation because it's the exact point where two or more bones meet. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T7#GNS121_U3_T7_h1)

question: What happens when a person suffers severe damage to their hippocampus?

options.A: They lose the ability to feel physical pain
options.B: They experience paralysis in their lower limbs
options.C: They forget all their childhood memories
options.D: They can no longer form new long-term memories

explanation: You nailed it! The hippocampus is needed to lock in new experiences into long-term storage, so damage makes forming new memories very difficult. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T13#GNS211_U3_T13_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of disaster monitoring in nursing?

options.A: Writing historical books about past weather events
options.B: Systematically collecting and analyzing data during crises
options.C: Punishing facilities that fail to prepare for emergencies
options.D: Replacing the role of physicians in emergency rooms

explanation: Disaster monitoring is all about watching, gathering, and studying information so healthcare workers can respond effectively to emergencies. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T2#GNS315_U5_T2_h1)

question: What usually happens when health professionals bypass community input and decide problems alone?

options.A: Government funding increases because the staff showed independence
options.B: The community completes all health projects much faster
options.C: They often target issues that do not match the real priorities of the residents
options.D: Local disease rates drop instantly due to professional expertise

explanation: Without local consultation, healthcare workers may focus on problems that matter to textbooks rather than the community. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h5)

question: If a patient suffers a ruptured ectopic pregnancy, what main substance builds up in her Pouch of Douglas?

options.A: Cerebrospinal fluid
options.B: Blood
options.C: Lymph fluid
options.D: Urine

explanation: Spot on! A tubal rupture causes internal bleeding, and since blood is a heavy fluid, it flows down to collect in that lowest pelvic space. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T27#GNS216_U5_T27_h2)

question: Who is the brilliant thinker behind the System of Profound Knowledge?

options.A: W. Edwards Deming
options.B: Abraham Maslow
options.C: Florence Nightingale
options.D: Jean Watson

explanation: W. Edwards Deming created this popular management framework to help leaders understand and improve organizational systems. You'll see this come up a lot in nursing management! [learn more](GST319_U2_T3#GST319_U2_T3_h1)

question: A patient has both hookworms and roundworms at the same time. What kind of drug property do you need?

options.A: Strict specificity for a single parasite enzyme
options.B: Ability to cross the blood-brain barrier easily
options.C: Broad-spectrum activity against multiple nematode species
options.D: Rapid elimination through the renal system

explanation: You got it! Broad-spectrum drugs are fantastic because they tackle several different worm species in one go. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T7#GNS223_U3_T7_h5)

question: What is the main function of the heart valves during the cardiac cycle?

options.A: To prevent blood from flowing backward
options.B: To generate electrical sparks for the heartbeat
options.C: To filter bacteria out of the bloodstream
options.D: To separate the left and right lungs

explanation: Valves act like one-way doors that open to let blood pass forward and snap shut to stop it from flowing backward. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h3)

question: You are helping a patient with severe bradykinesia get ready in the morning. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Withholding morning medication until physical therapy is finished
options.B: Allowing extra time for the patient to complete tasks independently
options.C: Completing all hygiene tasks quickly for the patient to save time
options.D: Restricting oral fluid intake to prevent frequent bathroom trips

explanation: Patience is key! Bradykinesia means everything takes longer. Giving them extra time keeps their dignity intact and encourages them to do as much as they can for themselves. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T4#GNS222_U4_T4_h6)

question: A patient recovering from serum sickness complains of stiff, aching joints. Which nursing action is best?

options.A: Apply ice packs to the joints for twenty minutes every hour
options.B: Massage the inflamed joint firmly to break up the immune complexes
options.C: Keep the affected limbs strictly immobilized in a rigid splint
options.D: Encourage gentle range-of-motion exercises as tolerated

explanation: Gentle movement is wonderful here; it keeps the joints from locking up while giving the tissues space to heal comfortably. [learn more](GST114_U4_T10#GST114_U4_T10_h7)

question: What does the word 'vesicant' mean when talking about certain chemo drugs?

options.A: Natural supplements that cure nausea caused by treatment
options.B: Solutions used to clean the skin before a surgical incision
options.C: Drugs that cause severe tissue damage if they leak outside the vein
options.D: Medications that are only given orally in pill form

explanation: Vesicants are tricky drugs! If they escape the vein into the skin, they can cause blistering and tissue damage, which is why nurses watch IV sites so closely. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T10#GNS321_U1_T10_h3)

question: Why are maternity homes so important in rural Nigerian communities?

options.A: They replace federal tertiary teaching hospitals completely
options.B: They eliminate the need for any medications during labor
options.C: They offer free surgical care funded by international donors
options.D: They serve as local bridges to care when distant hospitals are hard to reach

explanation: Spot on! By being close by, they bridge the gap so mums don't have to travel huge distances just to get basic care. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T15#GNS324_U5_T15_h1)

question: A patient asks why her injectable birth control takes months to wear off after her scheduled date. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: The medicine travels directly to the brain and stays in the neurons
options.B: The injection forms a slow-release depot store in the muscle tissue
options.C: The drug permanently alters the DNA structure of the ovaries
options.D: The liver stores the chemical in fat cells for future energy use

explanation: Injectables like DMPA are designed as a "depot" injection, meaning the muscle holds onto the medicine and releases it slowly into the body over a few months. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T17#GNS215_U6_T17_h3)

question: Why is nebulization often chosen over other inhalers for patients in acute respiratory distress?

options.A: It requires only normal, quiet breathing instead of a deep, forced inhalation.
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for any vital sign monitoring.
options.C: It stops all lung infections within minutes of starting the treatment.
options.D: It works ten times faster than any intravenous medication available.

explanation: Patients struggling to catch their breath cannot coordinate deep inhalers, making normal breathing through a nebulizer mask much easier. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h1)

question: Which type of vaccine contains a weakened form of a live germ?

options.A: Inactivated
options.B: Live-attenuated
options.C: Recombinant
options.D: Toxoid

explanation: Spot on! 'Live-attenuated' means a living germ has been weakened (attenuated) so it can safely spark a strong immune response. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T16#GNS215_U6_T16_h2)

question: What is the main goal of safe motherhood initiatives?

options.A: To minimize the total cost of obstetric medications
options.B: To ensure all births occur strictly inside tertiary hospitals
options.C: To reduce preventable maternal and newborn deaths
options.D: To completely eliminate pregnancy for high-risk women

explanation: You've got this! Safe motherhood is all about keeping both mum and baby safe and healthy by stopping complications before they get out of hand. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T001#GNS226_U1_T001_h1)

question: What does 'caregiver burden' mean in community mental health?

options.A: The physical weight of medical equipment kept inside the home
options.B: The physical, emotional, and financial strain experienced by family caregivers
options.C: The mandatory training hours required to become a certified nurse
options.D: The legal responsibility of paying for all hospital admission bills

explanation: You got it! Looking after a loved one with chronic illness at home can take a heavy toll physically and emotionally. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T3#GNS324_U4_T3_h7)

question: A community nurse notices a sudden weekly jump in new diarrhea cases in a local village. What should be done first?

options.A: Assume the data collection error is harmless and ignore it
options.B: Wait until the end of the year to calculate annual prevalence
options.C: Close all local schools permanently without further testing
options.D: Investigate possible sources like contaminated water supplies

explanation: Brilliant clinical thinking! A sudden spike means you need to hunt down the source—like bad drinking water—right away to stop the spread. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T11#GNS313_U1_T11_h6)

question: A study compares lung cancer patients with healthy people, looking backward at their past smoking habits. What kind of study is this?

options.A: Prospective cohort study
options.B: Qualitative ethnography
options.C: Case-control study
options.D: Randomized controlled trial

explanation: Think of a case-control study as looking in the rearview mirror. You start with the 'cases' (people who have the condition) and look backward at their past exposures compared to healthy controls. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T1#GNS224_U1_T1_h5)

question: Which animal is the main carrier of the Lassa virus?

options.A: Domestic house cat
options.B: Mastomys rat
options.C: Ground squirrel
options.D: Fruit bat

explanation: The multimammate rat (Mastomys species) is the natural reservoir that carries and spreads the virus without getting sick itself. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T8#GNS214_U1_T8_h2)

question: What is the primary effect of patriarchal structures on family health responsibilities?

options.A: Men take on all nursing duties at home
options.B: Children become responsible for their own care
options.C: Health and domestic matters are left entirely to women
options.D: Couples share all medical decisions equally

explanation: Patriarchal norms often assign all caregiving and domestic duties to women, keeping men away from health spaces. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h2)

question: Which event is most likely to trigger psychosocial stress in an older adult?

options.A: Participating in regular physical exercise
options.B: Gaining new hobbies in retirement
options.C: Loss of a spouse or close friends
options.D: Traveling to new community centers

explanation: Bereavement and the loss of peers are major life transitions that deeply impact the mental health of older adults. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T1#GNS321_U3_T1_h5)

question: What is considered the single most effective way to stop the spread of infections in a hospital?

options.A: Wearing heavy utility gloves all day
options.B: Frequent and proper hand hygiene
options.C: Administering prophylactic antibiotics
options.D: Changing bed linens every morning

explanation: Never underestimate the power of clean hands! Good hand hygiene washes away transient germs before they can travel from patient to patient. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T4#GNS122_U4_T4_h5)

question: A patient is grieving because a stroke has taken away their physical independence. How would a nurse describe this type of loss?

options.A: Anticipatory mourning
options.B: Complicated grief
options.C: Perceived loss
options.D: Actual loss

explanation: Even though others might not physically see it, losing your independence is deeply felt by the patient. That's what makes it a perceived loss! [learn more](GNS221_U4_T6#GNS221_U4_T6_h1)

question: What is the specific name of the stress ulcer that forms in the stomach due to severe burn trauma?

options.A: Zollinger-Ellison ulcer
options.B: Cushing's ulcer
options.C: Peptic ulcer
options.D: Curling's ulcer

explanation: Think 'Curling' up from belly pain after a burn! It's a classic stress ulcer caused by low blood flow to the stomach early in shock. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h8)

question: What fluid is found mainly inside the inner ear's membranous labyrinth?

options.A: Cerebrospinal fluid
options.B: Blood plasma
options.C: Perilymph
options.D: Endolymph

explanation: Endolymph is the special fluid that fills the inner compartments of the labyrinth to help us sense movement. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T8#GNS211_U4_T8_h2)

question: What is the medical term for trouble swallowing in advanced degenerative diseases?

options.A: Apraxia
options.B: Aphasia
options.C: Dysphagia
options.D: Ataxia

explanation: Dysphagia means difficulty swallowing. Spotting this early helps us protect patients from choking or getting food in their lungs! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T14#GNS222_U4_T14_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of a run chart in a healthcare setting?

options.A: To order hospital medical supplies
options.B: To calculate staff salary bonuses
options.C: To track data points over time
options.D: To diagnose rare medical diseases

explanation: Run charts display sequential data points on a graph to show how a specific process changes across a period of time. [learn more](GST319_U1_T3#GST319_U1_T3_h1)

question: A patient is recovering from major surgery and needs tissue repair. Which energy state is best?

options.A: Positive energy balance
options.B: Zero net energy balance
options.C: Complete metabolic shutdown
options.D: Severe negative energy balance

explanation: Healing takes work! Building new cells and repairing tissues require extra building blocks and calories, so a positive energy balance is just what the patient needs. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T006#GNS227_U4_T006_h6)

question: Why are older adults much more prone to bad drug interactions?

options.A: They experience reduced kidney and liver function along with polypharmacy
options.B: They routinely consume excessive amounts of herbal supplements
options.C: Their plasma protein levels are always abnormally elevated
options.D: Their digestive tracts absorb oral medications much faster than younger adults

explanation: As we age, our kidneys and livers don't clear drugs as quickly as they used to. Combine that with taking several medications at once, and drugs can easily build up to harmful levels. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T4#GNS215_U2_T4_h5)

question: Which hormone is primarily responsible for remodeling collagen and softening ligaments during pregnancy?

options.A: Relaxin
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Cortisol
options.D: Thyroxine

explanation: Relaxin is produced during pregnancy to soften ligaments and joints, preparing the pelvis for delivery. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h1)

question: What does a positive alkaline phosphatase test in a milk sample tell you?

options.A: The milk is completely sterile and safe to drink
options.B: The milk has been stored at freezing temperatures
options.C: Antibiotics were successfully added to the batch
options.D: Pasteurization was incomplete or inadequate

explanation: You're learning fast! Alkaline phosphatase is a natural enzyme that proper pasteurization destroys. If it's still active in the test, the milk wasn't heated correctly. [learn more](GST114_U3_T4#GST114_U3_T4_h6)

question: On the AVPU neurological scale, what does the letter 'V' stand for?

options.A: Voice
options.B: Ventilation
options.C: Vomiting
options.D: Vascular

explanation: Remember AVPU: Alert, Voice-responsive, Pain-responsive, and Unresponsive. It's a quick and handy way to check mental status! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T13#GNS321_U2_T13_h2)

question: What is one of the main goals of state-level health insurance schemes in Nigeria?

options.A: Increasing taxes on imported medical equipment
options.B: Eliminating all private pharmacies in urban centers
options.C: Reducing out-of-pocket spending on medical care for poor families
options.D: Providing free international travel for nurses

question: Which germs are the most common causes of Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID)?

question: Which of these is a classic example of a physical workplace hazard?

options.A: Repetitive wrist motion
options.B: Workplace bullying
options.C: Loud machinery noise
options.D: Hepatitis B virus

explanation: Physical hazards include environmental factors like noise, vibration, or extreme temperatures that can harm the body over time without direct chemical contact. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T5#GNS225_U7_T5_h2)

question: How do lipid-soluble hormones travel through the bloodstream to reach their target cells?

options.A: Encased in hard mineral capsules

options.D: Inside red blood cells alongside oxygen

question: Inside the testes, where does the actual creation of sperm take place?

options.B: Prostate gland
options.C: Seminiferous tubules
options.D: Bulbourethral glands

question: What is the classic description of the walking pattern often seen in late pregnancy?

options.D: A wide-based waddling gait

question: Which class of medication is usually given first for obsessive-compulsive neurosis?

options.D: Atypical antipsychotic medications

question: What is the main purpose of using a partograph during intrapartum care?

question: Which of these is NOT a benefit of knowing research classifications for a nurse?

options.D: Diagnosing complex medical conditions independently

question: What makes a histogram different from a regular bar chart?

question: A clinic is fully stocked with vaccines, but mothers refuse to bring their babies because nurses shout at them. What type of barrier is this?

options.A: Geographical distance barrier
options.B: Financial cost barrier
options.C: Environmental sanitation barrier
options.D: Attitudinal and service delivery barrier

question: A patient on trial leave stops taking their medication and acts aggressively at home. What is the main advantage of trial leave status?

options.A: The hospital automatically discharges the patient to a prison facility
options.B: The team must wait until the next court date
options.C: The family is fined for failing to supervise
options.D: The patient can be readmitted quickly without a complex new admission process

explanation: Because the patient is still officially connected to the hospital during trial leave, bringing them back safely and quickly is much easier if symptoms flare up. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h3)

question: What does "process monitoring" evaluate during a community health campaign?

options.A: The exact financial profit generated by local primary health clinics

options.C: The total number of hospital beds required for severe stroke patients
options.D: Day-to-day activities like attendance numbers and media broadcasts

question: A junior nurse listens to an experienced charge nurse mainly because 'that is how things have always been done here.' What type of authority is this?

options.A: Expert authority

question: Which of these is a clear example of an unsafe injection habit?

options.A: Using a contaminated needle to enter a single-dose medication vial

options.C: Dropping a used syringe straight into a safety box

question: What should a nurse do immediately after finding abnormal, life-threatening changes during an exam?

options.A: Delete the entry from the computer to avoid alarming others

options.C: Report the findings to the physician or charge nurse right away

explanation: Critical changes require prompt communication and action to ensure the patient gets emergency medical intervention quickly. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h7)

question: Why do patriarchal community norms negatively affect child health outcomes?

options.A: They restrict mothers from making independent medical choices for sick children
options.B: They encourage mothers to lead community health committees

options.D: They automatically increase the nutritional value of local foods

question: Why do nurses use the four-quadrant method during a quick abdominal assessment?

options.A: To quickly locate the general area of organ pain or discomfort

question: What is the main purpose of the watery fluid secreted in the small intestine?

options.A: To kill bacteria before they can reach the large intestine

question: Why might a community want smaller families on average, yet still have a low Contraceptive Prevalence Rate?

options.A: Excessive availability of free clinical staff in every village
options.B: Systemic barriers like supply stock-outs and spousal opposition
options.C: Natural biological immunity to pregnancy in rural populations
options.D: Universal rejection of modern medicine by community elders

explanation: Wanting a smaller family is one thing, but if clinics run out of supplies or partners object, women can't access the protection they want. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T027#GNS226_U6_T027_h3)

question: A patient asks you for antibiotics to treat a mild cold (a virus). How should you reply?

options.A: Advise the patient to take a double dose to clear the viral symptoms faster
options.B: Encourage the patient to find a different clinic that will prescribe the medication
options.C: Suggest saving leftover antibiotics from a previous prescription for this illness
options.D: Explain that antibiotics only treat bacterial infections and will not cure a virus

explanation: Wonderful nursing response! Patient education stops drug resistance in its tracks. [learn more](GST114_U2_T5#GST114_U2_T5_h6)

question: What is the main goal of psychiatric-mental health nursing?

options.A: Confining dangerous individuals to secure wards
options.B: Promoting health and caring for mental alterations
options.C: Prescribing long-term psychotropic medications
options.D: Isolating patients from community stressors

explanation: As psychiatric nurses, our heart is in holistic care—helping patients build wellness, easing distress, and supporting them through tough emotional times. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T2#GNS314_U1_T2_h1)

question: If you are posted as a nurse to a new displacement camp, what major environmental challenge should you expect?

options.A: Immediate surplus of specialized surgical equipment
options.B: Excessive availability of modern private housing
options.C: Complete absence of any communicable diseases
options.D: Overcrowding and limited access to clean water

question: Within how many hours must Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP) be started to reduce HIV risk after an exposure?

question: What is the main benefit of using a person-centred approach in post-abortion counseling?

options.A: It helps match birth control to the client's unique lifestyle and goals
options.B: It guarantees the patient will never feel any grief
options.C: It speeds up the clinic discharge paperwork
options.D: It forces the client to choose the strongest long-term method

explanation: Person-centred care is all about listening to what the patient wants. When they choose a method that fits their life, they are much happier using it! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T016#GNS226_U5_T016_h3)

question: Why should you avoid pouring harsh surgical scrubs directly inside an open wound?

options.C: It permanently stains the surrounding skin a bright yellow color

question: Which physical sign is most commonly associated with iron deficiency anemia?

question: What is the main sign of a post-dural puncture headache?

options.D: It is accompanied by sudden high fever

question: Why is early ambulation strongly encouraged after pelvic surgeries like a hysterectomy?

options.B: It forces the surgical incision to heal much faster
options.C: It restores immediate hormonal balance in the body
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for postoperative pain relief

explanation: Getting patients moving early promotes lower extremity circulation, significantly lowering the risk of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T7#GNS311_U1_T7_h6)

question: Why must the ear pinna be pulled downward and backward for a child under three years old?

question: A patient has been on strict bed rest for several weeks. What is likely happening to their bones?

options.C: Bone breakdown (resorption) is happening faster than bone building
options.D: Spongy bone is turning into solid metal-like columns

question: What is the primary goal of health education in primary health care?

options.D: To diagnose complex tropical diseases in the community

question: A community received many breastfeeding flyers, but clinic rates didn't improve months later. What should the nurse suspect?

question: Why is real-time, chronological documentation especially crucial in an emergency department?

question: What is a quick, thoughtful step to take before bringing a food tray to a patient's bed?

question: Why would a surgeon leave an amputation wound open instead of stitching the skin right away?

question: Which medication is commonly administered intrathecally to treat central nervous system involvement in certain cancers?

question: Why do many terminal patients and their families choose home-based palliative care?

question: How did modern safety acts like OSHA change workplace safety?

question: What is the most frequent cause of nephrotic syndrome in young children?

question: What is the most common cause of fever seen every day in Nigerian clinics?

question: How do public health policies regarding alcohol and drug sales help protect a community?

question: What should you do if an older resident has severe memory loss and cannot give informed consent for a procedure?

options.D: Consult the designated family surrogate decision-maker

question: What is the general outlook for a patient who gets steady medical and psychological care for OCD?

question: How do peer educators help drive the elimination of harmful practices at the village level?

question: What makes an infant's upper airway much easier to block compared to an adult's?

question: What is the standard safe temperature for storing most routine vaccines in a fridge?

question: What is a major cause of waterborne and vector-borne diseases in local communities?

question: What is a direct result of poor nutrition in an older adult going through rehabilitation?

question: A patient asks why their new antibiotic must be taken strictly with meals. What is the best way to explain this?

question: What is the specific function of the auditory association area?

question: An unconscious child with cerebral malaria is brought into the emergency ward. What is your very first nursing priority?

question: What is the primary way data is analyzed in quantitative research?

question: Which of these waste items goes into a rigid, puncture-resistant container?

question: What is the main focus of post-abortion care (PAC) services?

question: A patient who had a barium swallow two days ago reports no bowel movement, abdominal cramping, and bloating. What is the most likely cause?

question: A patient is given a strong opioid pain medication. Which assessment is most important for the nurse to perform shortly after?

question: On a standard muscle strength scale, what does a score of zero (0) indicate?

question: Why is qualitative feedback just as important as hard numbers when evaluating a health project?

options.D: It reveals whether the community has truly gained ownership and confidence

question: Why does fluid naturally collect in the Pouch of Douglas when there is pelvic bleeding or infection?

question: Why is a longitudinal design great for studying chronic illnesses like heart disease?

options.A: It costs almost no money compared to other study methods

options.C: It allows researchers to watch how the disease develops and progresses slowly over time
options.D: It requires only one afternoon of data collection at a clinic

question: What is a very common cause of acute (short-term) fatigue?

options.A: A recent viral infection or short-term sleep loss
options.B: Long-standing, unmanaged hypothyroidism
options.C: Advanced autoimmune joint destruction
options.D: A multi-year history of clinical depression

explanation: Exactly! Acute fatigue usually pops up suddenly from something clear and temporary, like fighting off a cold or pulling a late-night reading session for exams. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T3#GNS123_U3_T3_h3)

question: Why do nurses keep taking classes and training long after leaving nursing school?

options.A: To replace basic nursing school education completely
options.B: To guarantee an automatic promotion in the hospital
options.C: To fulfill mandatory paperwork for the ministry of health
options.D: To maintain and update professional knowledge and skills

explanation: Medicine and nursing change every day! Continuing education helps us stay sharp, keep our clinical skills fresh, and give our patients the best care possible. You've got this! [learn more](GST321_U8_T8#GST321_U8_T8_h1)

question: What forms the numerator in the standard prevalence formula?

options.A: Total number of existing cases
options.B: Number of newly reported deaths
options.C: Number of people who recovered
options.D: Total population size at risk

question: What defines an epidemic compared to an endemic disease?

options.A: Only children living in rural villages catch the illness
options.B: Cases rise significantly above the normal baseline level
options.C: Infections disappear entirely during the dry season
options.D: The disease spreads globally to multiple continents

explanation: An epidemic occurs when the frequency of a disease surges well past what is normally expected for that area and time. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T14#GNS313_U1_T14_h2)

question: What color do Gram-positive bacteria show up as under the microscope after a Gram stain?

options.A: Blue
options.B: Green

options.D: Purple

question: What is the golden rule for preventing needle-stick injuries after giving an injection?

options.A: Never recap used needles
options.B: Always recap needles using two hands
options.C: Bend the needle before throwing it away
options.D: Store used needles in your uniform pocket

question: What is a major nursing priority during the immediate postoperative period following a gynecological surgery?

options.A: Discontinuing all pain medication immediately

options.C: Monitoring vital signs for signs of hemorrhage
options.D: Initiating rigorous high-intensity aerobic exercise

question: Which of these is NOT a helpful way for a nurse to handle referral barriers?

options.C: Linking clients with local transport schemes or community support groups

question: What do we call the process where cancer cells break away and spread through the blood or lymph to other parts of the body?

options.A: Mitosis
options.B: Metastasis
options.C: Metaplasia
options.D: Apoptosis

explanation: You're doing great! Metastasis happens when malignant cells travel via blood or lymph to set up secondary growths in distant organs. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T5#GNS321_U1_T5_h3)

question: What usually happens when a hospital operates under a strict blame culture?

options.A: Patient satisfaction scores increase significantly
options.B: Staff members hide errors and near misses out of fear
options.C: Doctors and nurses collaborate more effectively
options.D: Clinical staff report every minor mistake immediately

explanation: Spot on! If people know they will be punished harshly, they naturally keep quiet to save their jobs—which puts future patients at risk. [learn more](GST319_U5_T3#GST319_U5_T3_h3)

question: What usually happens when the government health sector and voluntary agencies fail to communicate well?

options.A: Complete elimination of poverty in rural areas
options.B: Immediate reduction in community disease rates
options.C: Instant eradication of all infectious diseases
options.D: Duplication of health efforts and wasted resources

explanation: Well reasoned! Without good teamwork, two agencies might end up doing the exact same thing in one village while leaving another village completely ignored. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T28#GNS225_U5_T28_h6)

question: A patient with a broken hip is placed in skin traction mainly for which reason?

options.A: Preventing deep vein thrombosis in the affected leg

options.C: Permanent alignment so surgical repair is no longer required

question: Which clinical observation around the umbilical stump indicates the development of omphalitis?

options.C: Natural separation of the cord after one week
options.D: A small drop of clear blood upon diaper removal

question: What is the very first thing that happens during the initiation stage of cancer development?

options.D: A permanent mutation occurs in the cellular DNA

question: What is a common challenge hospitals face regarding waste management in resource-limited settings?

options.A: A complete absence of patients generating any hazardous waste

question: A hospitalized patient refuses to eat, avoids talking to staff, and expresses hopelessness about recovery. Which nursing conclusion is most accurate?

options.A: The patient is using problem-focused coping to solve their illness

options.C: The patient has successfully achieved the stage of resistance in GAS

question: Which test is most commonly used to check for structural causes of secondary dysmenorrhoea?

options.A: Brain CT scan

question: How do most electronic infusion pumps push fluid through the tubing?

question: Which chronic viral infections are most commonly linked to intravenous drug use?

options.A: Malaria and Yellow Fever

options.D: Influenza and Tuberculosis

question: A patient refuses birth control pills because she heard they cause permanent infertility. How should you reply?

options.A: Ignore her concern and write the prescription anyway
options.B: Explain that fertility returns quickly once pills are stopped
options.C: Tell her infertility is the price for effective protection
options.D: Agree with her and suggest only natural calendar tracking

question: Why are omega-3 fatty acids particularly important in the diet of a breastfeeding mother?

options.A: They support the infant's brain and nervous system development

options.C: They act as the primary source of daily energy for the mother
options.D: They prevent the mother from gaining too much postpartum weight

explanation: Omega-3 fatty acids, especially DHA passed through breast milk, play a major role in building the baby's brain and eyes. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T009#GNS227_U2_T009_h3)

question: If a patient's body has very low hormone levels for months, how will their target cells likely respond?

options.A: Receptor downregulation to conserve cellular energy

options.C: Receptor upregulation to increase cellular sensitivity
options.D: Complete destruction of the hormone production glands

explanation: When hormones are scarce, cells put out more receptors—like putting out extra fishing nets—to catch every little bit of hormone that floats by. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T11#GNS211_U1_T11_h2)

question: What is a very common result of high humidity inside an oxygen tent?

question: What is a common error that new administrators make during financial planning?

options.C: Spending all school funds exclusively on medical equipment
options.D: Refusing to accept government grants for school feeding

question: How is a physiological antagonist different from a regular receptor blocker?

options.C: It always causes a permanent chemical bond in the blood

question: Which brain chemical is most closely linked to the reward system and feelings of pleasure?

options.A: Thyroxine
options.B: Insulin

question: According to Maslow's pyramid of human needs, which level comes absolutely first?

question: What is the main job of Sertoli cells while sperm is being made?

question: You notice raw, red skin inside a patient's nostrils while getting ready to put on a nasal cannula. What should you do first?

question: What is the primary goal of palliative care in a long-term care setting?

question: Why is quarantine used as a public health tool during an outbreak?

question: When examining the tummy, why do we listen (auscultate) before we press (palpate)?

question: What are the two most common major causes of antepartum haemorrhage?

question: Why must the patient's fingers or toes be left uncovered at the end of the application process?

question: What is the main chemical trigger in your blood that tells your brain it is time to breathe?

question: Which of these actions breaks patient confidentiality during a home visit?

question: What is the main reason a researcher tries to control variables in a study?

question: Which of these counts as a biological water pollutant?

question: Why is asking about sexual health an important part of routine nursing care?

question: How does neural control of hormones differ from humoral control?

question: When is transformational leadership most helpful in a healthcare facility?

question: What is caregiver burnout?

question: Which of these is NOT one of the core pillars of safe motherhood?

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should do when turning an annoying ward problem into a research question?

question: Why is picking the right research design so important for your everyday patient care?

question: Why is male involvement important in family planning decisions?

question: What is a common reason why vaccines accidentally freeze inside a health clinic fridge?

question: What is a thyroid storm?

question: What is an important nursing intervention during a home visit to a patient with severe dementia?

question: You see a sudden, sharp spike on a monthly infection rate graph that is normally very flat. What should you suspect first?

question: What type of bowel prep is usually given right before a proctoscopy?

question: What is looked at first when choosing drugs for the Nigerian Essential Medicines List?

question: What should a home health assessment include besides vital signs and physical symptoms?

question: Which specific white blood cells are primarily targeted during acquired immune decline like HIV?

question: What is the nurse's main role when working alongside local faith-based support systems?

options.C: Coordinating care to bridge clinical needs with community spiritual resources

question: Why is it dangerous for a patient to rub their eye right after getting a numbing (anesthetic) drop?

question: A mother just gave birth six hours ago in the maternity ward. Which immediate postpartum emergency should you watch out for most closely?

question: How is an idiosyncratic reaction different from a regular side effect?

options.B: Contaminated hospital tap water
options.C: A nurse with a skin infection
options.D: A patient recovering from malaria

explanation: Well done! Things like water, soil, and medical equipment are non-living (inanimate) sources that can store and grow pathogens. [learn more](GST114_U2_T1#GST114_U2_T1_h2)

question: Why are methods like drama and town criers often preferred over printed pamphlets for health education?

options.A: Drama groups do not require any planning or preparation time
options.B: They accommodate varying literacy levels and engage local culture
options.C: They are the only communication tools approved by the WHO
options.D: Printed pamphlets are illegal to distribute in rural villages

explanation: Performance arts and verbal community channels ensure that everyone, regardless of reading ability, absorbs the health message. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T4#GNS124_U4_T4_h4)

question: Why is it so important for nurses to directly ask new mothers about leakage or pain during postnatal visits?

options.A: Hospital policy requires a written confession of any weakness
options.B: Postnatal hormones cause temporary memory loss regarding physical symptoms
options.C: Midwives are legally forbidden from physical examinations without questions first
options.D: Patients often feel embarrassed to bring up issues like leakage or pain on their own

explanation: Spot on! Many women suffer quietly because they think postpartum leaking is just 'normal now'. As nurses, we must gently check in on them. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T12#GNS121_U5_T12_h5)

question: How does a female condom stay securely in place inside the vagina?

options.A: A flexible inner ring at the closed end
options.B: Suction created by an external pump
options.C: Sutures placed by a healthcare provider
options.D: An adhesive strip on the outside

explanation: You nailed it! The inner ring at the closed end helps the user push and anchor the pouch securely inside. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h2)

question: Why is avoiding a fever important for a patient recovering from cardiac arrest?

options.A: Fever stops the heart from responding to standard medications
options.B: Fever increases the brain's need for oxygen and worsens injury
options.C: Fever causes the intravenous lines to clot off quickly
options.D: Fever makes it impossible to check the patient's blood pressure

explanation: Elevated temperatures speed up brain metabolism when brain cells are already vulnerable, leading to worse recovery outcomes. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T4#GNS315_U4_T4_h7)

question: When a local disaster strikes, who is almost always the very first responder?

options.A: International humanitarian workers
options.B: Specialized military rescue squads
options.C: Local community members themselves
options.D: Federal disaster relief agencies

explanation: You got it! Neighbors and local residents are already right there to help before official rescue teams arrive. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T11#GNS315_U5_T11_h5)

question: Why must you be careful when looking at a trend on a scatter diagram?

options.A: Graphs can only show data from fewer than ten patients
options.B: Correlation does not automatically prove cause and effect
options.C: Numbers on the axes change every time the page is refreshed
options.D: Visual plots cannot be used for clinical decision making

explanation: Just because two things move together on a graph doesn't mean one directly caused the other. Always keep your critical thinking cap on! [learn more](GNS217_U4_T12#GNS217_U4_T12_h2)

question: A nurse wants to show the percentage breakdown of different nursing specialties in a hospital. Which chart should be used?

options.A: Pie chart
options.B: Line graph
options.C: Scatter plot
options.D: Histogram

explanation: Fantastic! Pie charts are wonderful for showing parts of a whole, like slices of a cake representing different hospital departments. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T2#GNS217_U4_T2_h6)

question: What does the golden nursing rule 'if it wasn't documented, it wasn't done' mean in a court of law?

options.A: Unwritten care cannot be proven to have been given in a court of law
options.B: Verbal reports to doctors hold more legal weight than written notes
options.C: Documentation is more important than actually speaking to the client
options.D: Nurses do not need to perform procedures if they write about them

explanation: Legally, courts rely on written records. If an action is missing from the client's file, it is legally considered not to have happened! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T026#GNS226_U6_T026_h7)

question: How should a washed diaphragm be stored after it dries?

options.A: In its designated storage case away from heat and sunlight
options.B: Wrapped tightly in a plastic bag inside the kitchen freezer
options.C: At the bottom of a handbag without any protective covering
options.D: Hanging openly on a bathroom wall hook exposed to light

explanation: Keeping it in its cool, dark storage case protects the material from heat and sunlight, helping it last a long time. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T017#GNS226_U6_T017_h6)

question: You notice the safety box on your treatment trolley is about three-quarters full. What should you do?

options.A: Seal the container and replace it with a new one
options.B: Push the contents down firmly with a gloved hand to create more space
options.C: Transfer some needles into a regular black plastic bag
options.D: Leave it open until the end of the week to save money

explanation: Safety first! Never push down or overfill sharp containers. Seal them at three-quarters full to prevent accidental needle pricks. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of a stock card in a healthcare facility?

options.A: To record the daily vital signs and health status of admitted patients
options.B: To document the financial salaries and allowances of hospital workers
options.C: To schedule the duty shifts and off-days of the ward nursing staff
options.D: To track the exact quantity and movement of a specific supply item

explanation: A stock card functions as a ledger specifically designed to monitor inventory levels, showing when items enter and leave the ward. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h1)
